subject: International Business
notes: International business core. No numerical questions apply; extra objective and case items included.

questions.text: The exchange of goods services and capital across national borders is
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.explanation: International business involves cross border trade and investment.

questions.text: The increasing interconnection of world economies is called
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Globalisation is the growing integration of economies and markets.

questions.text: A business that operates in multiple countries is called a
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.explanation: A multinational company operates and invests in several countries.

questions.text: International business is riskier than purely domestic business
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.explanation: Cross border business adds currency political and cultural risks.

questions.text: List the drivers of international business
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.correctAnswer: Market seeking resource seeking efficiency seeking and strategic asset seeking motives.
questions.explanation: These motives drive firms to internationalise.

questions.text: Explain the importance of international business
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.correctAnswer: International business expands markets diversifies risk accesses resources and technology and enhances competitiveness and growth for firms and nations.
questions.explanation: Cover market expansion and resource access benefits.

questions.text: The theory that nations should produce goods they can make most efficiently is
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Adam Smiths absolute advantage holds that nations export what they make most efficiently.

questions.text: The theory that nations should specialise where their opportunity cost is lowest is
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Ricardo comparative advantage justifies trade on relative efficiency.

questions.text: The Heckscher Ohlin theory explains trade by differences in factor endowments
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Heckscher Ohlin links trade to relative abundance of factors of production.

questions.text: State the theory of comparative advantage
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: A nation benefits by specialising in goods it produces at a lower opportunity cost and trading for the rest.
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is the basis of mutually beneficial trade.

questions.text: Explain the mercantilist theory of trade
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Mercantilism held that a nation gains by maximising exports and minimising imports to accumulate gold and silver treating trade as a zero sum game.
questions.explanation: Cover the export surplus and bullion accumulation doctrine.

questions.text: Exporting goods directly to foreign customers is an entry mode of
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Exporting is selling goods produced domestically to foreign markets.

questions.text: Granting a foreign firm the right to use technology for a fee is
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Licensing transfers rights to technology or brand for a royalty.

questions.text: A wholly owned subsidiary is the entry mode requiring the highest investment
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: A wholly owned subsidiary involves full ownership and high commitment.

questions.text: List the modes of entering foreign markets
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Exporting licensing franchising joint venture and wholly owned subsidiary.
questions.explanation: These modes differ in control investment and risk.

questions.text: Explain the factors determining the choice of entry mode
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Entry mode choice depends on firm resources market size risk tolerance control desired and host country regulations.
questions.explanation: Cover internal capability and external market factors.

questions.text: The international body that regulates world trade is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The WTO sets and enforces rules of international trade.

questions.text: The institution that provides short term finance for balance of payments problems is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The IMF assists countries with balance of payments support.

questions.text: A tariff is a tax imposed on imported goods
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Tariffs are taxes on imports used to protect domestic industry.

questions.text: List the types of trade barriers
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Tariff barriers and non tariff barriers such as quotas subsidies and technical standards.
questions.explanation: Trade barriers divide into tariff and non tariff types.

questions.text: Explain the functions of the World Trade Organization
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: The WTO administers trade agreements provides a forum for negotiation settles disputes and monitors trade policies to ensure free and fair trade.
questions.explanation: Cover rule making dispute settlement and trade monitoring.

questions.text: The policy document that governs Indias exports and imports is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The EXIM policy sets the framework for exports and imports.

questions.text: The document that evidences the contract of carriage in shipping is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is a receipt and contract of carriage.

questions.text: A letter of credit is a guarantee of payment by the importers bank
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: A letter of credit assures the exporter of payment by the bank.

questions.text: List the documents used in export trade
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Commercial invoice bill of lading certificate of origin and letter of credit.
questions.explanation: These documents complete an export transaction.

questions.text: Explain the objectives of the EXIM policy
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: The EXIM policy promotes exports facilitates imports and balances trade to earn foreign exchange and support economic growth.
questions.explanation: Cover export promotion and trade balance objectives.

questions.text: The price of one currency in terms of another is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The exchange rate is the price of one currency in another.

questions.text: The market where currencies are bought and sold is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The forex market facilitates currency trading.

questions.text: Cultural differences can create barriers in international business
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Language customs and values differ across countries affecting business.

questions.text: Distinguish between a fixed and a floating exchange rate
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: A fixed rate is set by the government while a floating rate is determined by market demand and supply.
questions.explanation: The difference is who determines the exchange rate.

questions.text: Explain the role of culture in international business
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Culture shapes consumer behaviour negotiation styles and management practices so firms must adapt products communication and management to local cultures.
questions.explanation: Cover adaptation of marketing and management across cultures.

questions.text: Assertion: A weaker domestic currency boosts exports. Reason: A weaker currency makes domestic goods cheaper for foreign buyers
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Global finance forex and culture (assertion reason)
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: A weaker currency lowers the foreign price of exports raising demand.

questions.text: Match the entry mode to its characteristic
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Exporting requires the least investment while a subsidiary gives full control.

questions.text: The global institution that lends for long term development projects is the
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: The World Bank finances long term development projects.

questions.text: The set of agreements promoting free trade among member countries is a
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: A free trade area removes barriers among members.

questions.text: Explain the stages of internationalisation of a firm
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Firms internationalise through stages from exporting and licensing to joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries increasing commitment and control at each step.
questions.explanation: Trace the escalation of commitment across stages.

questions.text: Read the case: A firm exporting goods faces payment risk from a foreign buyer. Recommend a payment mechanism that reduces the risk
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: The firm should use an irrevocable letter of credit where the buyers bank guarantees payment against compliant documents.
questions.explanation: Apply the letter of credit to mitigate payment risk.

questions.text: Read the case: A company plans to enter a foreign market but lacks capital and local knowledge. Recommend an entry mode and justify it
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: A joint venture or licensing is best because it shares capital and risk and taps the local partners market knowledge.
questions.explanation: Match limited resources to a shared risk entry mode.

questions.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of globalisation
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Globalisation expands markets lowers costs and spreads technology but also increases competition interdependence and inequality between countries.
questions.explanation: Balance economic integration benefits against its costs.

questions.text: The risk that a foreign government may seize assets is political risk
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.explanation: Political risk includes expropriation and policy changes abroad.

questions.text: Explain the factors affecting exchange rates
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Exchange rates are affected by inflation interest rates balance of payments political stability and market speculation.
questions.explanation: Cover economic and political determinants of exchange rates.

questions.text: List the risks in international business
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.correctAnswer: Political risk commercial risk currency risk and cultural risk.
questions.explanation: These risks make international business more complex.

questions.text: Explain the meaning and importance of balance of payments
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: The balance of payments records all external transactions and reveals a countrys trade position currency pressures and need for policy adjustment.
questions.explanation: Cover the current and capital accounts and their significance.

questions.text: The term FOB means the seller bears cost up to the ship named by the buyer
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: FOB means free on board where the seller delivers goods on board the vessel.

questions.text: Explain the role of export promotion councils in India
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Export promotion councils assist exporters with market information trade fairs quality and policy inputs to boost exports of specific products.
questions.explanation: Cover the support functions of export councils.

questions.text: A company whose global strategy adapts products to each local market follows
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Localisation adapts offerings to local preferences and conditions.

questions.text: Explain the concept and types of trade blocs
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Trade blocs range from free trade areas and customs unions to common markets and economic unions with increasing integration among members.
questions.explanation: Describe the levels of regional economic integration.

questions.text: The duty levied on imports to protect domestic industry is a protective tariff
questions.subject: International Business
questions.explanation: Protective tariffs shield domestic producers from foreign competition.

questions.text: Explain the stages of economic integration
questions.subject: International Business
questions.correctAnswer: Economic integration proceeds from free trade area and customs union through common market to economic union with increasing harmonisation of policies.
questions.explanation: Trace the progression of integration stages.

questions.text: Explain the factors that determine international competitiveness
questions.subject: International Business
questions.topic: Nature and drivers of international business
questions.correctAnswer: Competitiveness depends on cost quality technology innovation and supporting institutions as captured in Porters diamond of factor conditions demand and related industries.
questions.explanation: Cover cost technology and Porters diamond determinants.
